fitter.text: A pump-fleet fitter has laid her tools out on a towel under the painted face. She taps her own chest, then points at yours.

win.text: She works without asking what you want. It aches. It fits.

swap.text: A boy in a fridge-door boat sorts salvage by touch, his eyes bandaged. He holds out a hand, palm up, and waits.

win.text: He weighs it, nods, and presses something else into your hand.

dice.text: Three people sit round a stove that isn't theirs, throwing chip casings like dice. One of them shifts over to make room.

win.text: The casings land your way. They pay without looking at you.

lose.text: The casings land wrong. Someone takes your money without looking up.

netted.text: A body hangs in the lowest net, face down in the water. Something still blinks at the back of its neck.

win.text: It comes free. The blinking stops when you take it.

lose.text: The net is wired. It bites before it lets go.

medic.text: An old woman sits among the cables with a medical kit open on her knees, its seal long broken. She holds up two stims and rubs her fingers together.

win.text: She counts the money twice and hands them over.
